comparison: Both strongly support the experimental design and scope claims (C1, C2, C22-C27). OpenEval emphasizes technical metrics like capture efficiency and sequencing depth (C28-C30), while peer reviewers focus on the impressive scope and resource value. High agreement on study design validation.

Both support the successful methylation manipulation (C31-C33). OpenEval provides detailed validation through bisulfite sequencing, while peer reviewers implicitly accept technical execution without raising concerns. Complete agreement on methylation efficiency.

Both support identification of regulatory regions (C34-C36) and validation approaches (C37-C43). OpenEval emphasizes statistical thresholds and quality controls, while peer reviewers highlight cross-dataset validation and convergence across cell lines. Strong agreement on regulatory activity detection.

Both support validation of mSTARR-seq approach (C37-C43). OpenEval details enrichment statistics and cross-cell-type validation, while peer reviewers affirm convergence across datasets and cell lines. Complete agreement on method validation.

Both support widespread methylation-dependent regulatory activity (C44-C47). OpenEval provides specific correlation coefficients and CpG density relationships, while peer reviewers affirm that methylation influences baseline activity and note the large fraction showing methylation effects. Strong agreement.

Both support findings on methylation-activated regions (C48-C49). OpenEval details TF motif enrichments for p53 and Tfcp2I1, while peer reviewers accept the broader methylation-dependence findings without specific critique of this subset. Agreement on these specialized findings.

Both support the nuanced finding that most RRBS sites lack regulatory function (C50-C56). OpenEval emphasizes the critical challenge to assumptions about commonly studied sites, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the valuable resource provided. Complete agreement with appropriate caveats about cell-type specificity.

Both support context-dependent regulatory activity findings (C57-C62, C64-C69). OpenEval provides detailed statistics on condition-specific elements and TF motif enrichments, while peer reviewers affirm that methylation influences responses to environmental stimuli. Strong agreement on environmental context importance.

Both support TF motif enrichment validation (C64-C66). OpenEval details Bonferroni-corrected significance for IFNA and dexamethasone pathways, while peer reviewers accept the broader environmental response findings. Agreement on biological relevance of condition-specific regions.

Both support that condition-specific regulatory activity predicts endogenous gene expression (C67-C69). OpenEval emphasizes statistical validation and enhancer-gene linkages, while peer reviewers affirm the connection between methylation and environmental responses. Strong agreement.

Both strongly support widespread methylation-environment interactions for IFNA response (C70-C76). OpenEval provides exceptional statistical support and mechanistic patterns, while peer reviewers describe this as 'very convincingly shown' and 'compelling evidence.' Complete agreement on this major discovery.

Both strongly support in vivo validation using human macrophage data (C77-C83). OpenEval details within-individual correlations and ISG15 effect size, while peer reviewers describe this as 'very convincingly shown' with baseline methylation predicting flu response. Complete agreement on validation strength.

OpenEval supports biological context for ISG15 (C84) with literature citation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this through their strong affirmation of the macrophage validation findings but do not separately evaluate this contextual claim.

Both address ELA-associated sites lacking regulatory function (C86-C92), but with different confidence levels. OpenEval finds claims supported with appropriate caveats about cell-type limitations. Peer reviewers initially raised concerns about the dex model for ELA, marking this as UNCERTAIN even after revisions addressed the issue. Partial agreement with acknowledged limitations.

Both address interpretation of ELA findings (C93-C95). OpenEval supports the biomarker interpretation with caveats about single cell type limitations. Peer reviewers remain UNCERTAIN about the ELA conclusions despite acknowledging careful discussion of limitations. Agreement on data but divergence on strength of interpretation.

Both support the acknowledgment of limitations (C96-C99). OpenEval finds these caveats appropriate and reasonable, while peer reviewers accept that authors discussed limitations carefully. Complete agreement that caveats are warranted and well-articulated.

Both support synthesis of methylation-environment interaction findings (C100-C106, with overlap on C101-C103, C109). OpenEval emphasizes widespread interactions and in vivo validation, while peer reviewers affirm support for epigenetic embedding theory and influence on environmental responses. Strong agreement on major implications.

Both support the balanced synthesis and resource value (C107-C109). OpenEval finds conclusions well-motivated about silent methylation differences and environmental context importance. Peer reviewers emphasize the dataset as a key community resource for functional interpretation. Strong agreement on broader impact and future directions.
